title: Complete endpoints and reduced cone of the actual integral projection
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$; put $A_n=R/(t^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum], not a datum assuming projection invertibility. Schemes are finite type over $k$ and their structure morphisms need not be separated. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified compactification projection map [def-exchange-projection], with compact-support functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,R)$ in the derived-complete integral convention [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put
$$S=Rf_!K\widehat\otimes_R^LL,\quad T=Rf_!(K\widehat\otimes_R^LLf^*L),\quad u=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:S\to T.$$
All the integral objects $Lf^*L$, $K\widehat\otimes_R^LLf^*L$, $Rf_!K$, $S$ and $T$ are bounded constructible and derived complete. Their finite reductions have bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals independent of $n$. In particular arbitrary integral $K$ here has uniformly finite-Tor reductions. Under the canonical operation comparisons, the derived reduction of the actual map $u$ at every $n$ is exactly $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}$ for $K_n=K\otimes_R^LA_n$, $L_n=L\otimes_R^LA_n$. A cone $C$ of $u$ belongs to the same complete constructible category and satisfies the derived identification
$$C\otimes_R^LA_n\cong\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}).$$
These are identifications in the derived category, including the map and its quotient transitions. No existence of a lift of independently chosen finite-level arrows, and no detection of equality of maps by reduction, is asserted.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat target representative. Mathlib DerivedCategory.right_fac represents the arrow into it by a right fraction. Resolve the source of that fraction by a flat-term K-flat complex, and compose the representing map; the roof equation gives the endpoint identity. TR3 identifies its signed cone with the given cone. Tensoring a cone is the cone of the tensored map, and the triangulated subcategory of acyclic complexes gives cone K-flatness. The universal reduction counit is invertible on that cone. Its representative normalization and naturality give the derived transition equation. The unrestricted and intrinsic ordinary quotient transitions agree by uniqueness of their pure-tensor formulas. The cone transition is the original two-summand cone map of the unrestricted transitions. The generic degreewise cone naturality computation, applied to the intrinsic transition after identifying it with the unrestricted one, proves its strict transition equation with the signed cone comparisons.
